title: The World Sold AI. Jakarta Sold Its Miners.
deck: IHSG fell on all five days, 3.71% to 5,146.326, and gave back two thirds of the week before. Four gold and copper miners made a third of the fall as metal prices slid on US rate bets and the global AI sell-off. The big banks held. Bank Indonesia raised its rate to 6.00% and the rupiah still set records. Wall Street's worst day came after Jakarta closed, so we stay cautious.
description: Indonesia weekly research for 16 to 20 November 2026. sections.title: Jakarta fell less than Asia's chip markets. That is not a reason to buy.

blocks.text: IHSG fell on every day of the week, 3.71% in all, to 5,146.326. That is 198.080 points, 67.38% of the previous week's gain. A week ago we said the rally was too narrow to chase. That call was right for the week, and none of the five signs that would have changed our mind showed up.

The losses sat at the commodity end of the index. Four gold and copper miners, AMMN, BRMS, MDKA and EMAS, took 63.66 points off IHSG, 32.14% of the fall. Gold fell about 9% over the week and copper slid with it, as bets on US rate rises and the sell-off in AI stocks hit metals. At the weekend before, President Prabowo had told his ministers that the state should get at least 70% of the benefit from every mining permit. The big banks barely moved. BBCA, BBRI and BBNI rose a little and BMRI ended where it started.

The pressure came from outside. Asia headed for its worst week since 2020 as the AI trade broke, and Taiwan fell 17.50%. Foreign investors sold a net Rp2,608.57bn of Indonesian shares and sold on every day. Bank Indonesia raised its rate by 25 basis points to 6.00% on Wednesday, against a market that expected no change. The rupiah still hit record lows on Thursday and Friday.

We stay cautious. The worst day on Wall Street came on Friday after Jakarta had closed. The S&P 500 fell 3.70% and the Nasdaq 100 5.61%, so IHSG starts the new week with a shock it has not yet priced. The hopeful news came on Monday, when Bloomberg reported that MSCI may not downgrade Indonesia after all. We weigh it in the last section. We would turn less cautious after a week with no new record low for the rupiah, a week of foreign net buying and a close back above 5,344.406, where this week began.

blocks.label: Checking last week's call
blocks.text: Our caution held, and the signposts all pointed the same way. We wanted foreign buying in four of the five largest stocks. Instead foreigners sold BBCA, BBRI, BMRI and TLKM, by our estimate, and bought only ASII. IHSG peaked at 5,385.138 on Tuesday, short of 5,488. The rupiah set new records after Bank Indonesia met. IDX said nothing new about the 9% cap, and at Friday's close BBCA made up 10.74% of IHSG and BBRI 10.64%. Regular trading fell to Rp9.00tn a day. Our downside line, a close below 5,027.964, held. Friday's low was 5,094.892.

sections.title: Five losing days, each sold from above the previous close

blocks.label: Exhibit 01
blocks.title: Five falls in a row, the deepest on Wednesday and Thursday
blocks.note: Select a date to inspect the closing observation. Lines join daily closes and show no intraday highs or lows.

blocks.text: Monday fell 0.44% and Tuesday 0.30%. Every day traded above the previous close at some point, and every day closed lower. The biggest rallies came on Tuesday and Wednesday, 1.21% and 1.31% at the high. Wednesday was Bank Indonesia's decision day. Bloomberg Technoz reported IHSG up 0.51% at 5,331.93 soon after the rate rise. It closed 1.07% down at 5,247.879. Thursday fell 1.02% and Friday 0.92% to 5,146.326, after a low of 5,094.892.

blocks.caption: Exhibit 02. Breadth by number of stocks, recomputed from IDX's counts

blocks.text: The fall was broad. 544 of 945 stocks fell, 57.57%, and 427 of them lost more than 2%. Stocks worth Rp4,616tn fell, 53.24% of the value in IDX's chart. IDX again printed the percentages of the two falling groups in each other's place, in both bars, so every share here comes from the counts.

sections.title: A third of the fall came from four miners

blocks.label: Exhibit 03
blocks.title: Five laggards and five leaders
blocks.note: Weekly IHSG points as IDX prints them on page 5. Our rebuild from index shares gives the same ten figures to within 0.01 point.

blocks.text: AMMN, the copper and gold producer, fell 14.13% and took 26.39 points, more than any other stock. BRMS fell 20.11%, MDKA 17.79% and EMAS 14.20%. Together the four took 63.66 points. Add ANTM, TINS and INCO and these seven miners took 75.72 points, 38.23% of the fall. The ten largest drags in IDX's table took 124.70 points, 62.95%. The leaders were small by comparison. BBCA added 4.98 points and EXCL, up 15.38%, added 3.78.

blocks.caption: Exhibit 04. The ten largest drags, and the foreign side of each

blocks.text: The selling was not all foreign. By our estimate foreigners sold BRPT, BRMS and TPIA hard. AMMN, the largest drag, is different. Foreigners sold an estimated Rp67.80bn of it on Monday and Tuesday and bought back Rp65.56bn from Wednesday, and the price fell about 7.3% in each half of the week, so foreign flow does not explain it. ASII fell 3.64% while foreigners bought an estimated Rp123.68bn of it. TLKM had the largest estimated foreign selling of any stock, Rp408.85bn.

blocks.caption: Exhibit 05. Competing explanations for the fall in miners and commodity stocks

blocks.text: We cannot pin the fall on one cause. Lower gold and copper prices fit the metal miners through the week, the 70% remark fits Monday, and MSCI's deletions fit BRMS and BRPT. They landed in the same week as a global sell-off, and we think the combination, not any one of them, explains how far these stocks fell.

sections.title: Commodities fell hardest, banks and healthcare held

blocks.label: Exhibit 06
blocks.title: Basic materials and energy led the fall
blocks.note: Weekly price changes of the IDX sector indices.

blocks.text: Basic materials fell 10.73% and energy 8.81%, and IDX's Commodity 20 index lost 13.27%. Financials slipped only 0.20% and healthcare rose 0.05%. The infobank15 index of banks rose 0.59%. Sharia indices, which leave out conventional banks, fell harder, the JII by 6.60%. The Acceleration Board, for small companies, fell 6.17%.

sections.title: Foreign selling on every day, banks included

blocks.label: Exhibit 07
blocks.title: Net selling of Rp2,608.57bn, Rp947.41bn of it on Friday
blocks.note: Official all-market stock trading, foreign purchases less sales. This measures trading, not money leaving or entering the country.

blocks.text: Official foreign net selling was Rp2,608.57bn, after net buying of Rp462.73bn the week before. It was heaviest at the end, and Friday's Rp947.41bn was 36.32% of the week. It was the heaviest week of selling since the week to 30 October. Foreign net selling for 2026 passed Rp100tn on Friday and now stands at Rp100.23tn.

blocks.caption: Exhibit 08. Estimated foreign net trading in selected liquid large caps, 16 to 20 November

blocks.text: Our estimate values IDX's daily foreign buy and sell shares at each day's close, across all markets. It sums to Rp2,591.10bn of net selling, Rp17.47bn less than the official figure, though single days miss by up to Rp99.33bn, so we use it to rank stocks and never as a total. Among 63 liquid large caps, worth Rp10tn or more with an average of Rp10bn or more of regular trading a day, foreigners sold 47 and bought 16. They sold an estimated Rp398.29bn of BBCA, BBRI and BMRI, yet all three ended flat or higher. Local buyers took the other side.

sections.title: Three one-off trades made up Rp10.53tn of turnover

rows: Half of Harum Energy passed between two holders under the same control
The controller bought back 26.667% under a repurchase agreement
The controller sold 29.87% to a new holder and kept control
Astra's voluntary tender offer, taking its stake to 84.947%
blocks.caption: Exhibit 09. Three single trades and a tender offer, from IDX's stock summary and the filings

blocks.text: IDX's headline shows turnover down 47.90% to Rp12.35tn a day, but the week before held the Rp66.81tn ADRO and AADI transfer. This week had large one-off trades of its own. Single negotiated trades in HRUM, WIFI and INET came to Rp10.53tn, 62.89% of all negotiated value, and none of them says much about value. The HRUM trade moved half the company between two holders under the same control, at the previous close. WIFI changed hands at Rp2,870, 3.48 times its close. The filings call it a buy-back under a repurchase agreement, and IDX's stock summary for 19 October fits a trade of the same 1,415,652,000 shares at the same price.

Regular-market trading, where prices are set, was Rp44.99tn, Rp9.00tn a day and 3.83% less than the week before. Foreigners made 33% of all trading, up from 19%, but both weeks held large one-off trades, so we read little into the change.

blocks.label: Correcting last week
blocks.text: Last week we wrote that without the ADRO and AADI transfer, foreigners made about 44% of trading. That was too high. IDX's pair table for 10 November shows local-to-local trading of Rp66,598bn, less than the Rp66,808bn transfer, while foreign-to-foreign trading jumped to Rp5,504bn, against less than Rp2,000bn on each other day. Part of the transfer was booked between foreign accounts. Allowing for that, the foreign share was about 36%, close to the 37% of the week before. We have corrected last week's note.

blocks.title: Foreigners sold Rp11.09tn to locals and bought Rp8.48tn from them
blocks.note: Ribbon width is the value traded, in Rp tn, from seller to buyer. The three one-off trades were between local holders.

sections.title: Asia headed for its worst week since 2020

blocks.label: Exhibit 11
blocks.title: Indonesia was 14th of 32 markets in IDX's table
blocks.note: Changes from IDX's global table. Asian rows run Friday to Friday. IDX takes European and American markets at their last close before its report, so those rows run from Friday 13 November to Thursday 19 November. IDX lists the US only through the Dow, so the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 rows use FRED closes for the same two dates.

blocks.text: Taiwan fell 17.50%, Korea 7.95% and Japan 7.70%. CNBC Indonesia, citing Reuters, reported Asia outside Japan on course for its worst week since March 2020 and Taiwan for its worst since August 1990. The chip markets fell hardest, but Jakarta's 3.71% was only middling for Asia, sixth of thirteen Asian markets in IDX's table. The Philippines, Singapore and Hong Kong, with few chip stocks, fell more. What kept Jakarta's fall from being worse was its banks, whose three largest names are 29.40% of the index. India was the only Asian market in the table to rise, by 2.85%.

In New York the S&P 500 fell 8.61% over the week and the Nasdaq 100 10.43%. CNBC put the slide down to the listing of Anthropic, which priced at $83, traded above $115 on its first day and ended the week at $88.91, and to Nvidia, which fell 14% on Friday after a report of an SEC probe into its accounting. CNBC Indonesia also points to the Anthropic listing and to US rates. The minutes of the Federal Reserve's October meeting record two members voting for a rise and many seeing the AI buildout as a material inflation risk, and CNBC quotes Governor Waller saying a half-point rise may be needed in December.

Treasury yields fell as money moved to safety, the ten-year to 5.04% on Thursday from 5.15% on the previous Friday. The VIX, Wall Street's gauge of expected swings, rose from 19.30 to 28.44 over the same days. CNBC cites CME data putting the chance of a US rate rise in December at 96%.

Metals fell too. Gold lost about 9% over the week, its biggest weekly fall since March, to its lowest since September 2025, according to both CNBC and Bloomberg Technoz, which put it down to bets on US rate rises and the AI sell-off. CNBC quotes a trader saying the equity sell-off forced some holders to sell gold to cover losses, while Bloomberg Technoz says the fall is hard to tie to visible sellers. Copper fell on a stronger dollar, rate bets and doubts about AI demand. COMEX copper dropped 5.30% on Wednesday alone, CNBC Indonesia reports, and Bloomberg Technoz says London copper was heading for one of its worst weeks in a decade.

sections.title: Bank Indonesia raised rates. The rupiah set records anyway

blocks.title: In dollars IHSG lost about 4.02%
blocks.note: The starting values use this week's IHSG and BI JISDOR. Move the sliders to try a different currency assumption. The equity close and the reference rate are taken at different times.

blocks.text: Bank Indonesia raised the BI-Rate by 25 basis points to 6.00% on Wednesday 18 November, with the deposit facility at 5.25% and the lending facility at 6.75%. It said the rise would steady the rupiah against growing global uncertainty and act early to keep inflation within its target of 2.5% plus or minus 1% in 2026 and 2027. Bloomberg Technoz reported that the market had expected a hold at 5.75%. The rupiah firmed for an afternoon.

JISDOR, Bank Indonesia's reference rate, ended the week at 18,278, 0.33% weaker. Every reading this week was weaker than the old record of 18,241 from 12 November, and Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday each set a new one.

Trade is not the problem. Bank Indonesia's figures, out on Friday, show the current account deficit shrank to US$2.0bn in the third quarter, 0.5% of GDP, from US$12.6bn. The strain is in portfolio money. In the third quarter less foreign money went into government bonds, and in the fourth quarter up to 16 November the central bank counts US$0.9bn leaving the stock market, even as government global bonds and sukuk brought total net inflows to US$4.80bn. A strong dollar, US rate bets and foreign selling of shares push on the rupiah, and one rate rise has not stopped them.

sections.title: Three paths, and what would change our view

blocks.label: After the close: MSCI
blocks.text: On Monday morning Bloomberg reported that MSCI's chief executive, Henry Fernandez, told President Prabowo on a 10 November call arranged by Ray Dalio that MSCI did not necessarily intend to downgrade Indonesia, and would keep advising officials on what they need to do. In October MSCI threatened to move Indonesia two steps down, from emerging to standalone. The steps reportedly discussed include taking people with political ties off the board of OJK, the financial regulator, and clearer rules on the high-concentration list and on changes to the LQ45 index. Kontan carried the report the same morning. It rests on people who asked not to be named, MSCI has not confirmed it, and Bloomberg says MSCI plans its final decision by the end of June 2027. If it holds, it lifts the largest threat over foreign money in Jakarta, which is why it sits in our first path.

blocks.caption: Exhibit 14. Three paths for the coming weeks. Scenarios we can test, not forecasts

blocks.text: We lean to the second path for the next two weeks. Foreign selling was heaviest at the end of the week, Bank Indonesia's rise did not stop the rupiah's slide, and the worst US day came after Jakarta closed. Against that, Jakarta's banks held, the market trades at 10.65 times earnings, the current account deficit has shrunk, and Bloomberg's MSCI report, if MSCI confirms it, would lift the biggest weight on foreign money. So inside the index we would rather hold the banks than the miners, and we would not yet buy the index itself.

blocks.caption: Our tests for the coming weeks

blocks.text: On the downside the line stays at 5,027.964, the low of the week to 13 November. A close below it would undo all of that week's rise. Below 4,904.287, the close of 3 November, IHSG would be at its lowest close since this weekly began in September. With the three largest banks now 29.40% of the index, foreign selling of BBCA, BBRI and BMRI is what we would watch first.

blocks.label: What this note cannot see
blocks.text: We have no daily gold or copper prices from a primary source, so the link between metal prices and the miners rests on weekly figures from the press. Our stock-level foreign figures are estimates. They come within Rp17.47bn of the official total for the week but miss single days by up to Rp99.33bn. And we have no figure for selling by funds that track MSCI or IHSG, so we cannot size the index effect on BRPT and BRMS.

sourceIntro: Checked on 23 November 2026. Market data end at the 20 November close in Jakarta and in New York. IDX statistics, IDX and KSEI filings, Bank Indonesia, the Federal Reserve, FRED, S&P Dow Jones Indices and Nasdaq are primary sources. The main press facts rest on two outlets: CNBC with CNBC Indonesia for the global sell-off, CNBC with Bloomberg Technoz for gold, CNBC Indonesia with Bloomberg Technoz for copper, and Katadata with Bloomberg Technoz for the president's remark on mining. The MSCI report after the close rests on Bloomberg alone, which Kontan carried, and the text says so. Where only one outlet gives a detail, the text names it.
